hello.note: Also: Hallo. Casual: Heisann! or Hei hei! Formal, e.g. in an office: God dag.

goodbye.note: Short and very common: Ha det! Casual: Hei hei! or Snakkes! (talk soon).

please.note: Can sound pleading. In everyday requests Norwegians add takk instead: En kaffe, takk.

thank_you.note: Warmer: Tusen takk (a thousand thanks) or Takk skal du ha.

youre_welcome.note: Also common: Ingen årsak. When handing something over, say Vær så god.

yes.note: To say yes to a negative question, use jo: Kommer du ikke? – Jo!

sorry.note: Also very common: Beklager. For real regret: Jeg er lei for det.

excuse_me.note: Often just Unnskyld, followed by your question: Unnskyld, vet du hvor stasjonen er?

good_morning.note: Casual: Morn! Many people also use Morn as a quick hello later in the day.

how_are_you.note: Norwegians say du to almost everyone; the formal De is now rare. Also: Hvordan går det?

im_fine.note: Shorter: Bra, takk! To ask back: Og du?

whats_your_name.note: The h in hva is silent: 'va HAY-ter doo'. Du is polite enough, even with strangers.

my_name_is.note: Jeg sounds like 'yai'. More formal: Mitt navn er …

nice_to_meet_you.note: Often just: Hyggelig! Also common: Hyggelig å hilse på deg.

where_from.note: The h in hv- words is silent: hvor sounds like 'voor'.

speak_english.note: Most Norwegians speak English well. Start politely: Unnskyld, snakker du engelsk?

dont_understand.note: Also common: Jeg skjønner ikke. To ask someone to repeat: Hva sa du?

speak_slowly.note: Norwegian softens requests with litt (a bit) rather than a word for please. Also: langsommere.

where.note: Said 'voor'. Where to? is hvor hen? Where from? is hvorfra?

what.note: Said 'va'. Hva? alone can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say Unnskyld? or Hva sa du?

when.note: Å sounds like the 'aw' in law: 'nawr'.

why.note: Said 'VOOR-for'. Also common in speech: Hvorfor det?

who.note: Said 'vem'. Don't mix it up with hvor (where).

where_bathroom.note: Casual: Hvor er doen? Signs say WC; Damer = women, Herrer = men.

can_you_help.note: The h in hjelpe is silent: 'YEL-peh'. Extra polite: Kunne du hjelpe meg?

what_time.note: Also written and said: Hva er klokken? Both are correct.

what_means.note: Also common: Hva vil det si?

one.note: With neuter nouns it is ett: ett glass. Written én when stressed, to tell it from the article en.

seven.note: Syv is also correct and very common in speech.

eight.note: Å sounds like the 'aw' in law: 'AW-teh'.

water.note: Tap water is good to drink. In a café: Kan jeg få et glass vann?

bread.note: The d is silent: 'brø'. Ø is like the vowel in French deux.

menu_please.note: Kan jeg få …? is the everyday polite way to ask for anything. Short form: Menyen, takk.

bill_please.note: Short form: Regningen, takk. For the whole table: Kan vi få regningen?

delicious.note: Also: Deilig! or Nydelig! About a whole meal: Dette var kjempegodt!

no_meat.note: Or: Jeg er vegetarianer. Kj is a soft hiss, like the ch in German ich.

enjoy_meal.note: A host often says Vær så god! (help yourself). After eating, guests say Takk for maten!

right.note: Not 'correct', which is riktig. Turn right: Ta til høyre.

straight_ahead.note: Also spelt rett frem. Both are correct.

stop_here.note: Also very natural: Du kan slippe meg av her (you can let me off here).

airport.note: Official names and signs often use lufthavn, as in Oslo lufthavn.

hotel.note: Double l, stress on the end: ho-TELL.

train_station.note: In everyday speech: togstasjon, or just stasjonen. Oslo's main station is Oslo S.

want_to_go.note: Norwegian can drop the verb go here. Also very common: Jeg skal til … (I'm going to …).

is_it_far.note: Also: Er det langt herfra? (from here)

one_ticket.note: Return ticket: tur-retur. In many cities you buy tickets in an app.

too_expensive.note: Haggling is not usual in Norwegian shops, except at flea markets (loppemarked).

cheaper.note: Asking about the shop's range: Har dere noe billigere? (dere = you, plural)

id_like_this.note: For a neuter noun: dette. When buying, also common: Jeg tar denne.

just_looking.note: Also: Jeg bare ser meg litt rundt.

pay_card.note: Cards are taken almost everywhere, and some places no longer accept cash.

cash.note: To pay in cash: betale kontant.

closed.note: Signs also say Lukket. Most shops are closed on Sundays.

big.note: With neuter nouns: stort (et stort glass). Plural: store.

small.note: Irregular: lite with neuter nouns (et lite glass), små in the plural.

tomorrow.note: Morgen alone means morning. Tomorrow morning: i morgen tidlig.

later.note: Also spelt seinere. Afterwards: etterpå. Soon: snart.

good_evening.note: Hei works at any time of day, too.

good_night.note: Also said when parting late at night. Leaving earlier in the evening: Ha en fin kveld!

see_you_later.note: Also: Ses senere! Tomorrow: Vi ses i morgen! Casual: Snakkes!

wait_moment.note: Also: Bare et øyeblikk. Casual: Vent litt!

every_day.note: The h is silent: hver sounds like 'vair'.

call_police.note: In Norway dial 112 for the police, 113 for an ambulance, 110 for the fire brigade.

need_doctor.note: Lege is used for both male and female doctors.

im_lost.note: On foot. When driving: Jeg har kjørt meg vill.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: Jeg er ikke helt i form. Ill: Jeg er syk.

hospital.note: Out of hours, for urgent but not life-threatening problems, go to the legevakt.

lost_phone.note: Mobil is the everyday word for a mobile phone. Telefonen also works.

allergic.note: E.g. allergisk mot nøtter (nuts), melk (milk), gluten.

be_careful.note: Sudden warning: Pass på! or Se opp!

i_like_it.note: About food, also: Det smaker godt.

dont_like_it.note: Also common: Det liker jeg ikke.

im_happy.note: Glad is the everyday word for happy. Deeply happy: lykkelig.

congratulations.note: On a birthday: Gratulerer med dagen!
